title: Never skip the modelled write-up
statement: Once a procedure has been modelled in full, let learners skip its earlier modelled steps, but always play the step that models the written answer in full.
example: In one design the write-up is the fourth step in all nine of its procedures, so the skip rule needs no exceptions.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design's skip rule is that the child may skip the modelling moment but not its fourth step, the write-up, which plays in full until the modelled response has been read aloud, because the written expectation is the thing being modelled (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 285 and 415). Skipping the first three steps is the default once a procedure has been modelled once (line 303). One procedure's steps were reorganised, adding a search step and retiring a refining one, so that the write-up is the fourth step in all nine of the design's procedures and the rule needs no exceptions (line 307).
against: Another record bars young learners from skipping instruction on their own judgment; this design makes skipping the first three modelled steps the default once a procedure is known and frames it as the child's option, removing the choice only after a lesson where the child was not secure (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 285, 303 and 87).
